newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Analysts say SNB move confirms market trend.
newsitem.headline: Analysts say SNB move confirms market trend.

text.p: Swiss franc short rates fell sharply after the Swiss National Bank (SNB) said it is cutting its discount rate by half a percentage point to 1.00 percent.
Market analysts said the move confirmed a trend already evident in the money market, and underscored the SNB's intentions to keep money rates low.
Swiss short-term money market rates have been lately trading below the discount rate.
"What we have seen in the latest few days is that the money market rates have come back sharply," said Matthias Denzler, market analyst at CS Research.
"The discount does not have much meaning. I see that (the latest cut) as a measure showing that the SNB will follow a relatively expansive policy," Denzler said.
"I would expect that the SNB will clearly try to avoid that rates rise. This will make clear to the market that the current policy will remain intact," Denzler said.
"On the one hand, it is only a confirmation. But on the other hand, it is also an affirmation," Denzler said.
The move caused the prices of short-term rates to surge, while bond prices also moved higher but to a lesser degree.
Manfred Gutmann, senior economist at Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS), said he was not surprised by the cut.
"In the past week short-term rates for three-month have been at 1.3 to 1.5 percent. It was clear the discount rate should be lower than these short-term market rates," he said.
He said this was more a psychological signal than something that would have a direct impact on market rates.
"This is a signal that they will continue their relatively strong supply of money...The signal is they want the Swiss franc exchange rate lower," Guttman said.

"I don't think this this will have a special effect on the Swiss franc exchange rate. It should stay around the current level. and move toward 83 francs per 100 marks for the rest of this year and the first three months of next year," he added.
Asked about the real economy, Guttman said he expected no measurable impact from the rate cut.

He said UBS was sticking to a forecast that the franc will weaken slightly over next three to six months, with short-term rates below two percent, bond yields at around 4 percent, and GDP growing 0.8 percent in 1997 after contracting 0.6 percent this year.
CS Trading Research director Gerard Piasko said he expected both dollar/Swiss and mark/Swiss to consolidate at higher levels in the short term, then seek further gains.
The dollar should consolidate above 1.2500 Swiss francs this week and try for the 1.2600 level next week if U.S. data show a stronger American economy, Piasko said.
He forecast a mark move to 82.35 mid-term.
On the real economy, Piasko said the rate cut would not help stimulate flagging private consumption but would support exports and investments.

"As the problems of the Swiss economy are clearly structural, as in Germany, we see this move as kind of supportive but not decisive in ending the trend of recessionary GDP quarterly figures," Piasko said.
